newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Jan oil products deliveries off 0.2 pct - API.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Jan oil products deliveries off 0.2 pct - API.

text.p: U.S. petroleum products deliveries slipped 0.2 percent in January to 18.167 million barrels per day from 18.212 million bpd a year ago, the American Petroleum Institute said Wednesday.
Products deliveries were flat partly because distillate deliveries fell 2.3 percent to average 3.60 million bpd in January from 3.68 million bpd a year ago.
The API cited warmer weather reducing heating oil demand and a buildup of stocks in previous months.

Distillate inventories finished January - usually the peak of the heating season -- at 114.8 million barrels, down 8.8 percent from December 1996's 125.9 million, but up 1.5 percent from January 1996's 113.1 million.

Gasoline deliveries increased 1.7 percent to average 7.380 million bpd from January 1996's 7.254 million, but the API said it did not believe that represented a marked shift from the recent trend of about a 1 percent growth rate.
Gasoline stocks ended January at 204.7 million barrels, up 5.1 percent from December's 194.8 million, but down 4.3 percent from January 1996' 213.8 million.

Kerosine jet fuel deliveries rose 0.5 percent to 1.613 million bpd from 1.605 million bpd a year ago, with growth limited by slightly warmer temperatures reducing the the amount of the fuel used for diesel winterization.
Residual oil deliveries plunged 17 percent to 847,000 bpd in January from 1.020 million bpd a year ago, continuing the winter's trend that could set a new recent-year low for residual oil deliveries.
Deliveries of other oils rose 2.3 percent to 4.771 million bpd from 4.666 million bpd a year ago.

Total petroleum imports including products slipped 0.2 percent in January to average 9.252 million bpd from 9.272 million a year ago, with a slight rise in crude imports more than offset by a drop in products imports.
The API said 1996 import data showed Canada replaced Saudi Arabia as the number two source of imports, after Venezuela.
Domestic crude production rose 0.2 percent to 6.460 million bpd from 6.449 million bpd a year ago as an increase in the lower 48 states offset Alaska's decline.
Refinery use was at 90.1 percent of capacity, down from 90.6 percent in January 1996, partly from a drop in distillate production.
